headline.text: Health costs are set to rise the most since

subhead: Most employers are bracing for another big renewal. Here’s what’s driving it, and the levers that work beyond raising deductibles.

heroCard.title: 2027 renewal outlook
heroCard.subtitle: Average projected cost increase per employee

section1.title: What’s driving the increase
section1.lead: National surveys point to the same handful of forces. Most of them are outside any one employer’s control, but not all.

cards.label: Specialty drugs
cards.title: GLP-1s and beyond
cards.body: Rising GLP-1 use alone is estimated to add about a full percentage point to 2027 cost growth, alongside autoimmune and cancer therapies.

cards.label: High-cost claims
cards.title: The big claims got bigger
cards.body: Catastrophic claims were the most-cited driver of 2027 increases in one national employer survey, ahead of specialty drugs.

cards.label: Provider prices
cards.title: Bigger systems, bigger bills
cards.body: Health system consolidation and lower government reimbursement are pushing higher prices onto employer plans.

cards.label: Doing nothing
cards.title: The status quo is expensive
cards.body: Employers estimate their current plans would cost about 11% more in 2027 if they made no changes at all.

levers.title: Levers that work beyond raising deductibles

items.title: Rethink the funding model
items.body: Level-funded, self-funded, and captive arrangements can return surplus and give you the claims data a fully insured plan rarely shares.

items.title: Put pharmacy under a microscope
items.body: Pharmacy is about a quarter of spend for many large employers. Transparent pricing, specialty programs, and biosimilars add up.

items.title: Set a clear GLP-1 policy
items.body: Decide coverage on purpose: clinical criteria, prior authorization, and pairing coverage with lifestyle support.

items.title: Manage the high-cost claims
items.body: Strong stop-loss terms, early case management, and centers of excellence for complex care protect the budget.

items.title: Design to steer, not just shift
items.body: Lower cost-sharing for high-value care and preferred sites can save more than raising the deductible for everyone.

items.title: Know your data
items.body: You can’t manage what you can’t see. Claims and pharmacy reporting belong in every renewal conversation.

questions.title: Renewal meeting questions
items: How much of our increase is market trend, and how much is our own claims?
Do we receive claims and pharmacy data, and in what detail?
Would a different funding model fit us now or in the next few years?
What are our stop-loss terms, and what’s excluded?
How is our pharmacy priced, and who keeps the rebates?
